sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Tennessee, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Saturday, October 24Passed

Your request must be received by your county election commission no later than 10 days before the election: Saturday, October 24, 2026. Requests are taken no earlier than 90 days before. Counties warn that waiting until the last day makes it hard to get the ballot and mail it back in time. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your county election commission must receive the ballot by the time polls close on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A ballot that arrives later is not counted. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Thursday, October 29, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Tennessee’s own page on voting by mail

At school away from home, in Tennessee or in another state? What Tennessee says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

Yes. To vote by mail you must fit one of the reasons in state law, and you name it on your request. The reasons include: you are 60 or older; you will be outside your county for all of early voting and all day on Election Day; you or your spouse are a full-time student at an accredited college or university in Tennessee outside your county (a student at school in another state qualifies under the 'outside your county' reason); you are in the hospital, ill or physically disabled and cannot go to your polling place, or you care for someone who is; your polling place is not accessible for your disability; you are a candidate; jury duty; working as an election official; a religious holiday during early voting and Election Day; you or your spouse hold a commercial driver's license or TWIC card and will be working out of state or county with no out-of-county address for mail; you are in the military or an overseas citizen; or you are on the permanent absentee list. People who live in a nursing home or assisted living facility inside their own county vote there with visiting election officials instead. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • By mail. Send a written request signed by you to your county election commission. It must include your name, home address, Social Security number, date of birth, the address to mail the ballot to, the election, your reason, and your signature. Many counties post a request form for the November 3, 2026 election. (official page)
  • By e-mail. E-mail the same request to your county election commission as an attached document that shows your scanned signature. Fax is no longer accepted. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Return it only by mail or a delivery service (U.S. Postal Service, FedEx, UPS or a courier). You may not hand-deliver it, fax it or e-mail it. (official page)

What the envelope needs

Sign the affidavit that comes with the ballot. No witness is listed in the county instructions read for this check. The request needs your Social Security number and signature. If you registered by mail or online and have not voted in your county before, you must vote in person the first time, unless you are on the permanent absentee list, in the Safe at Home program, or a military or overseas voter. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Tennessee’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Wednesday, October 14, 2026 to Thursday, October 29, 2026.

Early voting in person for the November 3 election runs Wednesday, October 14 through Thursday, October 29, 2026 (dates as posted by the Davidson County Election Commission; check your own county's hours and places). (official page)

Students

At school in Tennessee, away from home

County election offices say students do not gain or lose a residence by going to college away from home, so students register at their permanent home address ('Where's home?' is the question Davidson County suggests). A student registered at home who goes to college elsewhere in Tennessee can vote early or on Election Day at home, or ask the home county for a mail ballot. A student who now considers the college town home (for example, with a Tennessee driver license and car registered there) may register there. If you registered online or by mail, you must vote in person the first time; if you registered in person with your county election commission, you may vote by mail the first time. (official page)

At school in another state, with Tennessee as home

A Tennessee resident at school in another state qualifies for a mail ballot under the reason 'outside the county during the early voting period and all day on Election Day' (Hamilton County's guidance). Ask your county election commission to mail the ballot to your school address, and mail it back so it arrives before polls close on Election Day. The first-time-voter rule (vote in person the first time if you registered online or by mail) still applies. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military members, their spouses and dependents, and overseas citizens use the Federal Post Card Application, sent by mail or e-mailed with a scanned signature by 10 days before the election (Saturday, October 24, 2026); it also counts as a temporary registration and covers every regular election that calendar year. The ballot can be sent by mail or e-mail, but the voted ballot must come back by mail and be received by the close of polls on Election Day. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is a backup. (official page)

Tennessee in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The request deadline (10 days before the election) and the end of fax requests come from a recent change in state law (effective January 1, 2026, as Hamilton County's military page describes it).
  • October 24, 2026 is a Saturday; ask your county election commission how it handles requests that day.
  • Each request covers one election only, unless you are a military or overseas voter or on the permanent absentee list (which needs a doctor's statement).
  • Once you have asked for an absentee ballot, you can vote in person for that election only by provisional ballot (Shelby County Election Commission).
  • At early voting or on Election Day, bring an acceptable photo ID. College IDs are not accepted for voting in Tennessee (Davidson County's student FAQ).
  • A student away at school in Tennessee who still needs to register can register in person at the election commission in the county where the school is; that office dates it and forwards it to the home county, and the student can then ask for a mail ballot (Davidson County's student FAQ).
  • A student from another state at school in Tennessee who now considers Tennessee home may register here; one who considers another state home should register there and ask that state about voting by mail (Davidson County's student page).
  • Military and overseas ballots must arrive by 8 p.m. Eastern / 7 p.m. Central on November 3, 2026 (FVAP's 2026 Tennessee guide).

How this was checked

  • The Secretary of State's own site (sos.tn.gov) refused this check's requests, so these facts come from three county election commissions (Hamilton, Shelby, Davidson), which follow the same state law. The state's absentee guide is linked as the official page but was not opened here.
Where this comes from: 7 pages of Tennessee’s election office, its laws and the federal guide

  4. College Student Voter Registration, Davidson County Election Commission (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  5. Military & Overseas Absentee, Hamilton County Election Commission (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  6. Tennessee 2026-2027 Voting Assistance Guide, Federal Voting Assistance Program (U.S. Department of Defense) (federal guide; read October 21, 2026)
  7. College Student Frequently Asked Questions, Davidson County Election Commission (official page; read October 21, 2026)

Checked October 21, 2026. Rules and dates can change: Tennessee’s election office, and your county or local election office, have the final word.

Polls close at 7 p.m. Central time and 8 p.m. Eastern time, the same moment. Each county sets its opening time. (source)

    Anyone in line when the polls close may still vote.
